title.full: ASEAN Green Future Project Phase 2.2 Report, Optimization of Laos's Power Generation Sector

publisher.full: Sustainable Development Solutions Network and ClimateWorks Centre

description: Business-as-usual pathway with significant hydropower and coal use.

coreDrivers.policies: Hydro capacity additions in 2030 is aligned with NDCs, then additional additions are included based on ressource potential assessment.
coreDrivers.macroeconomicDrivers: SSP2 GDP, medium population growth extracted from World Bank and sectoral value-added trends from country target drive electricity demand.
coreDrivers.otherDrivers: Hydropower resource potential is the main constraint for end-year capacity mix.

dependencies.dependency_description: Current policy is implemented through fixed capacity assumptions: hydropower expands toward the assessed resource potential with a 2030 targets aligned with NDC while coal remains in the system through 2050. The pathway therefore does not use policy to eliminate coal.
The regulatory framework is represented mainly through national plans and standards, not detailed market design or permitting.

EP follows the existing-policy build-out rather than a least-cost solution. Cross-border electricity trade with Thailand is economically important, but the pathway does not provide forward-looking trade volumes or prices that determine the EP outcome.

EP imposes demand-side adoption assumptions exogenously, including passenger EV penetration of 30% in 2030 and 60% in 2050 and lower electric-truck uptake. These assumptions increase power demand but are not framed as a power-sector bottleneck.

EP expands significantly hydro capacities. Hydropower facilities are typically situated in isolated regions and require integration with the national system to distribute energy nationwide. However, EP does not quantify transmission expansion or model grid integration as a constraint.
Hydropower maxiumum potential ressources is reached by 2050 and is the limit to hydro expansion in Lao.

Seasonal water availability affects hydropower adequacy in the dry season. Laos power grid is already dependant on Thailand during that period. EP does not introduce a future change in hydrology or an environmental constraint on hydro deployment. EP therefore proceeds using the stated hydro potential without modelling future ecosystem/climate impacts.
The electrical system requires substantial human resources for its operation. This is not measured in this analysis.
